A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Batched NSGDM research. The complete main text and Appendices A–D support reliable matching of algorithms, mathematical statements, proofs, and presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical convergence bounds, proofs, and an analytic example in Appendix A. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical study and adds mathematical arguments and discussion. No original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 remains unchanged. Remark 3.1 generalizes the optional sign-based update from a shared stepsize eta_t to coordinate-specific eta_t,i, a limited procedural change to the existing alternative.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or reports empirical task evaluations. Both address the same nonconvex optimization setting with known or unknown tail index and generalized noise assumptions.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator set changes. SGD and Clipped SGD remain theoretical comparisons; the added Kornilov discussion compares mathematical inequalities rather than evaluated algorithms.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Algorithm 1's theorem-specific stepsizes, momentum choices, batch-size formulas, and iteration budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. Appendix A's analytic example is retained; the new appendix material supplies theoretical arguments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Expectations and probability bounds are mathematical statements.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains empirical scores or observations. The principal convergence-rate expressions and their parameter dependencies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds Equation (7) and a two-direction equivalence argument connecting Assumption 2.2 to global exponential smoothness, replacing v1's stronger-assumption argument. Theorem 3.3 explicitly adds the initial-gap bound and initialization at zero, with supporting calculation in Appendix D.2. v2 also expands Theorem D.1's parameter-substitution argument, specifies integrability in Lemma 4.3, and corrects the initial-gap definitions in Lemmas 4.1 and D.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: optimal convergence without clipping, a refined parameter-dependent lower bound, convergence with unknown tail index, and analysis under generalized assumptions.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix B reverse the assessment of removing prior L1 knowledge: v1 expects stronger smoothness to be necessary, whereas v2 argues removal is feasible under Assumption 2.2. Exponential dependence on L1 remains a tradeoff, and no complete L1-free convergence theorem is added. Appendix C also newly explains the claimed generality of its martingale inequality.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is added or removed. The main algorithm and its parameter prescriptions are retained; the additional details concern mathematical proofs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu, Jagabathula and Zhou (2023a) to support the deterministic-rate comparison, connects Appendix B to Chen et al.'s function class, and compares Lemma 4.3 with Kornilov et al.'s inequality. The Kornilov reference dated 2024 in v1 and 2023 in v2 is the same work.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and terminology edits, adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author information, and expands appendix explanations. The main narrative, section ordering, and overall appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript is reformatted throughout into ICLR style, changing fonts, margins, title and author arrangement, running headers, heading styles, and equation and algorithm layout. Neither version contains figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: Appendix B corrects v1's overly restrictive L1 discussion with a local-to-global smoothness argument. Explicit initialization and gap conditions in Theorem 3.3, corrected definitions, and expanded proof steps improve precision and checkability. These are focused gains: the central guarantees remain unchanged, and the L1-free extension still lacks a complete convergence theorem.
